source_name: Zakon o javnim nabavkama Crne Gore (consolidated text, Paragraf.me)
why_relevant: Consolidated Montenegrin Public Procurement Law text. Defines which bodies count as naručilac (including the Central Bank), publication obligations, thresholds and appeal deadlines — i.e. it tells the collector what MUST be published, where, and within what time windows, which is the basis for detecting missing/under-published notices.

source_name: Pošta Crne Gore – Javne nabavke (state-owned operator with payment/financial services)
why_relevant: The state postal operator provides retail payment and money-transfer services and runs a large counter network; its own procurement page publishes tenders for counter/POS, cash-handling and IT systems. A frequently overlooked buyer of payment infrastructure outside the banking licence perimeter.

source_name: Payten – News & Events (Asseco/ASEE payments arm, Montenegro operations)
source_subtype: vendor press release / customer reference feed
why_relevant: Payten is the dominant ATM/POS and card-acceptance vendor in Montenegro (present since 2006, own service centres, stated long-term partnerships with 9 of 11 Montenegrin banks). Its news feed names specific Montenegrin bank customers and go-lives (e.g. SoftPOS at Hipotekarna banka), which is the clearest public trace of private-bank buying decisions.

source_name: e-mon Servisni centar (ASEE Montenegro digital-banking service centre)
why_relevant: ASEE's Montenegrin e-banking service centre publicly lists its bank customers — NLB Banka, CKB, Prva banka Crne Gore, Erste Bank, Ziraat Bank, Lovćen banka, Universal Capital Bank, Addiko Bank, Adriatic Bank. This is effectively a live customer-logo map of the OfficeBanking/mobile/web-banking stack across nearly the whole private banking sector.

source_name: ASEE / Asseco South Eastern Europe corporate site
why_relevant: Parent of e-mon and Payten; publishes regional case studies, product lines (core banking, card management, digital channels) and investor reporting that occasionally names Montenegrin contracts. Central node of the Montenegrin bank-supplier ecosystem.

source_name: Finextra press-release archive (vendor announcements naming Montenegrin banks)
why_relevant: Fintech trade wire that carries vendor-issued press releases; confirmed to contain at least one Montenegro deal (CKB selecting Misys/Finastra FusionBanking Essence for digital channels). Searchable archive is a systematic way to surface vendor-side disclosures about private Montenegrin banks.

source_name: Finastra (ex-Misys) customer/case-study pages
why_relevant: Confirmed supplier to CKB Banka (FusionBanking Essence digital channels). Vendor case-study and customer pages are the natural place for follow-on Montenegro references and renewals.

source_name: Halcom – list of banks using Halcom (e-banking / qualified digital certificates)
why_relevant: Halcom publishes the roster of banks running its Hal E-Bank corporate e-banking and certificate infrastructure — an explicit vendor customer list covering the Adriatic region, useful for establishing Montenegrin installed base and for tracking displacement (Erste Bank Montenegro is publicly migrating off Halcom to eMon OfficeBanking).

source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica – Halcom to eMon OfficeBanking migration notice
why_relevant: Bank-side customer-communication pages are an under-used disclosure channel: they name the outgoing and incoming vendor platform explicitly. This one documents a concrete supplier switch inside a private Montenegrin bank.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. (regional card processor, SEE bank clients)
why_relevant: Slovenian processing hub serving banks across six SEE countries; its platform announcements (e.g. migration to Diebold Nixdorf Vynamic Transaction Middleware, 2024) change the processing stack for its client banks. Relevant for identifying whether Montenegrin banks outsource processing regionally rather than in-house.

source_name: Erste Group Card Processor (EGCP)
why_relevant: Group-internal card processor for Erste entities in CEE, with stated presence covering Montenegro. Explains why Erste Bank Podgorica's card processing may never surface as a third-party contract, and is the pointer to group-level processing decisions.

source_name: Visa Partner Directory (Visa Ready certified partners, incl. issuer processors)
why_relevant: Filterable directory of certified issuer processors, POS/acceptance and fintech partners by capability and region — a systematic way to enumerate which vendors are certified to serve Montenegrin issuers/acquirers, rather than guessing from press releases.

source_name: Mastercard partner / vendor directories (Engage, acceptance and processing partners)
why_relevant: Scheme-side partner enumeration equivalent to Visa's; a first-principles source because certification is a precondition for serving banks, so the directory reveals the eligible supplier pool even when no deal is announced. Not yet verified for Montenegro-specific filtering.

source_name: Montenegrin Foreign Investors Council – member list (MFIC)
why_relevant: Business-association membership roster that includes both banks and their technology suppliers (Payten confirmed as a member). Membership pages carry company profiles stating Montenegro market position and client counts — a compact way to enumerate the foreign supplier ecosystem serving private banks.

source_name: ICT Cortex – Montenegrin ICT cluster member directory
why_relevant: Cluster of Montenegrin software firms (Amplitudo, Bild Studio, Čikom, Logate, Codepixel, Fleka, Oykos, Data Design and others) categorised by capability including BI/data. Several of these firms build and maintain systems for Montenegrin banks, so the directory is the entry point to the domestic supplier layer that never appears in international vendor press.

source_name: Logate d.o.o. (Montenegrin software house serving banks)
why_relevant: Explicitly states it implements and maintains software systems for banks and telecoms in Montenegro and the region. Its references/clients pages are a direct window into domestic bank IT supply that no procurement portal covers.

source_name: Čikom d.o.o. (Montenegrin ICT integrator)
why_relevant: One of Montenegro's largest ICT integrators (70+ specialists), positioned in digital transformation and infrastructure; a plausible infrastructure supplier to banks. LinkedIn page carries project posts and partner-vendor badges (a proxy for which OEMs it resells).

source_name: Banksoft (regional core banking / SaaS core banking vendor)
why_relevant: Regional (HR/BA/RS) core banking vendor marketing SaaS-cloud core banking to smaller and branchless banks — exactly the profile of Montenegro's smaller private banks (Lovćen, Universal Capital, Adriatic, Zapad banka). Its solution and reference pages are a candidate source for Montenegrin core-banking wins.

source_name: eKapija Montenegro – business/investment portal and company catalogue
why_relevant: Regional business portal with a company catalogue (confirmed entries for ASEE Solutions/Asseco SEE) plus tender and business-news feeds. Serves both as an actor-mapping directory for suppliers and as an early-warning feed for contracts and partnerships in Montenegro.

source_name: Google Play / Apple App Store listings for Montenegrin bank apps (vendor fingerprint via bundle IDs)
why_relevant: App package identifiers leak the underlying platform vendor: NLB ProKlik Crna Gora ships under 'hr.asseco.android.jimba…', i.e. Asseco's Jimba/mToken mobile framework. Systematically enumerating bundle IDs, developer accounts and SDK signatures for all Montenegrin bank apps yields a vendor map that no press release provides.

source_name: CBCG Register of Banks (anchor list of the 11 licensed private banks)
why_relevant: Not a supplier source itself, but the authoritative denominator for this cell: the complete, current list of licensed banks whose vendor relationships must be mapped. Every vendor-side search and app-store fingerprint pass should be driven off this list.

source_name: Portal Analitika – IT sector / outsourcing regulation coverage
why_relevant: Covers the Montenegrin regulation of bank outsourcing/externalisation — the legal frame governing how banks select, contract and monitor IT suppliers. Bridges the A3 regulatory topic to the vendor-ecosystem cell and points to which supplier arrangements banks must document.
